# Analytical statements: implementation and numerical verification

<!-- Generated by `python -B scripts/verify_theory.py --write-doc`; `make verify` checks that it is current. -->

Every definition, lemma, proposition, theorem and corollary of the main text, the Supplementary Lemma 3 (work bound of Algorithm S3) and the equations whose arithmetic the lifecycle executes have an explicit reference implementation in [`cm_theory/`](../cm_theory/) and a numerical check in [`cm_theory/verification.py`](../cm_theory/verification.py). Each check draws randomized instances of the statement's hypotheses (random graphs including periodic ones, random states, bounded loss distributions, finite decision processes, budgets and cost bounds) with a fixed seed and tests the conclusion; identities are tested to floating-point precision and Monte Carlo coverage statements against the nominal level plus three binomial standard errors. Where an executable component of this repository implements the statement, the check runs that component: `cross_morse.statistics.empirical_bernstein` for Theorem 2, `cm_experiments.budget.run_budget_episode` for Lemma 3 and the Holm adjustments of the runtime and of the campaign tools.

```bash
make theory           # quick battery (seconds); part of make verify
make theory-full      # larger samples
python -B scripts/verify_theory.py --only theorem-2 --json-output "$REPORT_ROOT/theory.json"
```

Scope: a passing check shows that the implementation, the printed constants and the stated assumptions agree on the instances drawn. It is not a proof (the proofs are in Supplementary Notes S8-S26), it does not test whether a statement's hypotheses hold for a trained backbone, and it makes no claim about predictive benefit. The arithmetic of the manuscript's derived table entries is checked separately by `scripts/check_paper_constants.py` and `scripts/check_si_identities.py` (`make si-check`).

## Statements and verified claims

### Definition 1: Adapter-instrumented frozen GNN and supported model class

*Source:* main Section 2; Supplementary Tables S5b-S5c.

Registry action A0 reproduces the native aggregation (0.3 I + 0.7 P on the shared plants); at an inserted site V_a(H, R) = (1 - tau_a) H + tau_a [(1 - alpha_a) T_a H + alpha_a R] with tau_A0 = 0 a literal bypass, and every V_a preserves a common node state (affine weights sum to one).

Verified:

- registry A0 equals the native shared aggregation 0.3 I + 0.7 P
- native (rho, nu, alpha) of A0 is (0, 0.70, 0.25) (Table S5b)
- A0 at an inserted site is a literal bypass
- every inserted-site map V_a preserves a common node state (affine weights sum to one)

*Scope:* Operator level only; the E1 tolerance test of the trained plants (Table S5c) needs the run archives.

### Lemma 1: Executed transport validity

*Source:* main Eq. (8); Supplementary Notes S8-S14.

If every kernel is nonnegative and row stochastic, w lies in the simplex and 0 <= nu <= 1, then T = (1 - nu) I + nu sum_m w_m K_m is nonnegative and row stochastic; every registered action is a polynomial in P with nonnegative coefficients summing to one.

Verified:

- convex kernel mixtures with lazy mass are nonnegative and row stochastic
- every registered operator polynomial has nonnegative coefficients summing to one
- every registered transport matrix is nonnegative and row stochastic on random graphs

*Scope:* Floating-point tolerance 1e-11 on row sums.

### Lemma 2: Mass-corrected truncated resolvent

*Source:* main Eqs. (9), (21).

For 0 < eta <= 1 both K_eta = eta [I - (1 - eta) P]^{-1} and K~_{eta,T} are nonnegative and row stochastic, and ||K_eta - K~_{eta,T}||_inf <= 2 (1 - eta)^{T+1}; exactly, K_eta - K~_{eta,T} = (1 - eta)^{T+1} (P^{T+1} K_eta - I).

Verified:

- K_eta and K~_eta,T are nonnegative and row stochastic
- ||K_eta - K~_eta,T||_inf <= 2 (1-eta)^(T+1)
- K_eta - K~_eta,T = (1-eta)^(T+1) (P^(T+1) K_eta - I) exactly
- registered truncation bounds 2(1-eta)^9 at T = 8 *(reference value)*

*Scope:* Dense references on graphs of up to a few dozen nodes, including periodic (bipartite) random walks.

### Eq. (10): Executed range, reach and identity quantities of the registry

*Source:* main Eq. (10); Supplementary Tables S6 and S6b.

h_a = nu [(1 - rho) + rho sum_t t eta (1 - eta)^t], the identity mass (1 - eta)^{T+1} and the identity coefficient (1 - nu) + nu rho [eta + (1 - eta)^{T+1}] equal the moments of the executed operator polynomial; the maximum reach is T for a resolvent action and one otherwise.

Verified:

- executed range equals the first moment of the operator polynomial
- identity coefficient equals the P^0 coefficient
- maximum reach is T for resolvent actions and one otherwise
- main text: A0 moves 0.70 hops with identity 0.30; A7 moves 0.60 hops with identity 0.57

*Scope:* Table S6b values themselves are checked against the registry by scripts/check_paper_constants.py.

### Proposition 1: Deterministic replay equivalence

*Source:* main Section 2; Supplementary Notes S8-S14.

For a fixed graph, input, frozen model and deterministic sensors and policy, the realized closed-loop action sequence replayed open loop yields identical hidden states and predictions.

Verified:

- open-loop replay of the realized closed-loop sequence is bitwise identical
- instances in which the feedback rule switched actions *(reference value)*

*Scope:* Exact (bitwise) equality on dense float64 plants; GPU nondeterminism is outside the statement.

### Proposition 2: Fixed-mode finite-depth perturbation

*Source:* main Eq. (22); Supplementary Notes S8-S14 and Table S22.

e_{l+1} <= beta_l [e_l + M_l eps_l^op] + R_l e_l^ref with beta_l = L_LN (1 - alpha_l) L_phi ||W_l||_2 and M_l = ||H~_l||_{inf,2}; the product-sum bound follows by unrolling, and the frozen-head CE-with-logits change per node is at most sqrt(2) ||W_head||_2 e_L.

Verified:

- every realized step satisfies e_{l+1} <= beta_l [e_l + M_l eps_l] + R_l e_ref
- the unrolled product-sum bound holds at the final depth
- iterated recursion equals the product-sum form
- frozen-head CE change per node <= sqrt(2) ||W_head||_2 e_L
- ||grad_z CE||_2 <= sqrt(2)

*Scope:* Checked on the layer-normalization-free member of the class (L_LN = L_phi = 1 with ReLU); the local layer-normalization factor is a separate assumption.

### Proposition 3: Action stability

*Source:* main Eq. (23); Supplementary Table S21.

If every score is L_J-Lipschitz in the state and the gap between the best and second-best supported actions is m(s), the selected action is unchanged whenever 2 L_J ||s - s~|| < m(s).

Verified:

- the minimizer is unchanged whenever 2 L_J ||s - s~|| < m(s)
- the constant 2 is attained: a perturbation of m/(2L) + eps flips the minimizer

*Scope:* The factor two is shown to be tight for fixed action sets. Runtime use additionally requires invariant support, recovery, budget masks, site type and search decisions; these are not certified by this scalar helper.

### Theorem 1: Finite-family supported selection

*Source:* main Eqs. (19), (24)-(25); Supplementary Algorithm S4 and Table S20.

For a declared candidate domain and its feasible subset Q_feas, on the simultaneous coverage event every member of Q_s (hence q_M) satisfies Delta(q) < -eps_R and Delta(q) <= min_{Q_feas} Delta + eps_eq + 2 r_max, unless the comparator is returned.

Verified:

- on the coverage event every member of Q_s improves by eps_R and is near-best within eps_eq + 2 r_max in the declared candidate family
- max-t radii cover the family simultaneously (nominal 0.975)
- runtime nested selection agrees with the explicit feedback_only reference on its terminal Eq. (19) rule

*Scope:* Simulated families with Gaussian estimation error and max-t radii; coverage itself is a property of Algorithm S4 on the real units. The reference defaults to Eq. (3)'s feedback-only domain and also checks an all-feasible diagnostic, using the same family for selection, coverage and the guarantee. The candidate-domain contract across Eqs. (3), (18)-(19) and Table S11 remains unresolved. The current runtime uses feedback-only eligibility; its terminal rule is compared with the reference on synthetic nested-selection outputs, including metric/resource exclusions and failed observations. This is not a coverage proof for the real bootstrap.

### Theorem 2: Independent-graph clipped-loss admission

*Source:* main Eqs. (26)-(27); Supplementary Table S13.

For i.i.d. clipped paired differences in [-B, B], Pr(mu_clip <= U_a) >= 1 - delta_a with U_a = D_bar + sqrt(2 S^2 log(2/delta_a)/J) + 14 B log(2/delta_a)/(3 (J - 1)); the clipped fraction obeys f B^2 <= (J - 1) S^2/J + D_bar^2 deterministically.

Verified:

- Pr(mu_clip > U_a) <= delta_a on bounded i.i.d. units
- clipped fraction f <= [(J-1) S^2/J + D_bar^2]/B^2 deterministically
- J^-1 sum D_j^2 = (J-1) S^2/J + D_bar^2
- cm_theory admission bound equals cross_morse.statistics.empirical_bernstein

*Scope:* Monte Carlo coverage on bounded distributions (two-point, uniform, frequent small gains with rare large harms); the i.i.d. graph assumption is part of the statement.

### Corollary 1: Lifecycle error budget

*Source:* main Section 2; Supplementary Note S16.

On E_s and E_a, probability at least 1 - delta_s - delta_a, either q_D = q_C or the selection clause of Theorem 1 and mu_clip(q~_M) <= U_a <= -eps_a hold together; the confirmation map adds no term.

Verified:

- deployed and the joint selection-admission statement false: rate <= delta_s + delta_a

*Scope:* Simulated lifecycles with independent selection and admission samples; per dataset only. The reference declares feedback_only scope and checks Theorem 1 on the selector's same effective family.

### Corollary 2: Minimum admission sample size

*Source:* main Eq. (28); Supplementary Note S16.

U_a <= -eps_a requires J >= 1 + 14 B log(2/delta_a)/(3 (|D_bar| - eps_a)); equality is possible at zero sample variance, correcting the manuscript's strict-bound edge case. The numerator constant is 2.045 nats at B = 0.10, delta_a = 0.025.

Verified:

- every admitted configuration satisfies J >= 1 + 14 B log(2/delta)/(3(|D_bar| - eps_a))
- numerator constant 14 x 0.1 x log 80 / 3 = 2.045 nats
- Note S16: second penalty term 0.227, 0.066, 0.032 nats at J = 10, 32, 64
- Note S16: J - 1 > 341 at |D_bar| = 0.0090 and 1364 at 0.0045 (eps_a = 0.003)

*Scope:* Printed counts are compared with the registry by scripts/check_paper_constants.py and scripts/check_si_identities.py.

### Proposition 4: Value of state information

*Source:* main Section 2; Supplementary Note S16.

Every policy whose realized sequences lie in the supported family satisfies Delta(pi) >= Delta_oracle, with equality only if it attains the per-input oracle almost everywhere; Delta(q_D)/Delta_oracle lies in [0, 1] when Delta(q_D) <= 0.

Verified:

- Delta(pi) >= Delta_oracle for every policy inside the supported family
- the per-input argmin attains the oracle
- Delta(q_D)/Delta_oracle lies in [0, 1] when Delta(q_D) <= 0

*Scope:* Finite families of sequence losses.

### Proposition 5: Equal-compute break-even under the ensemble law

*Source:* main Eq. (29); Supplementary Tables S26 and S26b.

Under l(E) = l_inf + D_inf/E, q_D improves on the comparator at equal compute iff |Delta| > D_inf o/(E (1 + o)).

Verified:

- q_D beats the equal-compute comparator iff |Delta| > D_inf o/(E(1+o))
- least squares recovers (l_inf, D_inf) exactly from noiseless E14 grid data
- noisy fits fall within four standard errors

*Scope:* The law itself is an assumption that E14 measures.

### Definition 2: Deployment exchange rate and amortization horizon

*Source:* main Eq. (30); Table 2; Supplementary Table S23b.

lambda* = |Delta| / (E C(q_D) - C(q_C)); a deployer pricing work at lambda prefers q_D iff lambda < lambda*, and qualification is amortized to a share theta of the added work after M* = 3600 C_qual / [theta (E C(q_D) - C(q_C)) t_nom] inputs.

Verified:

- net benefit |Delta| - lambda dEC > 0 iff lambda < lambda*
- amortized qualification <= theta dEC iff M >= M*

*Scope:* Identities; the printed Table 2 values are checked by scripts/check_paper_constants.py.

### Proposition 6: Band-limited sensitivity and alignment identity

*Source:* main Eqs. (6.1)-(6.2); Supplementary Note S17 parts (i)-(v); Figure S18c.

||(T_a - T_a')X||_F <= [sum_b s_aa'b^2 P_b(X)]^{1/2} in the symmetric frame; the row-stochastic realization adds d_min^{-1/2}; windows satisfy |P_b - ||G_b X||^2| <= eps_b ||X||^2; retention and reference terms add as in (iv'); the alignment identity (6.2) is exact at the registered eps; the Chebyshev recurrence equals the dense window and a Gaussian sketch has relative SD <= sqrt(2/k).

Verified:

- ||(g_a - g_a')(L) X||_F <= [sum_b s_aa'b^2 P_b(X)]^(1/2)
- row-stochastic realization obeys the bound with d_min^(-1/2)
- T_a H = D^(-1/2) g_a(L_sym) D^(1/2) H
- |P_b(X) - ||G_b X||^2| <= eps_b ||X||^2 for the registered degree-8 windows
- the NumPy reference three-term recurrence on -S equals the dense window g_b(L)
- window approximation errors eps_b of the six registered windows *(reference value)*
- an L_U-Lipschitz update bounds the state displacement by L_U ||(T_a - T_a')H||_F
- mean CE over N nodes changes by at most sqrt(2/N) ||W_head||_2 ||dH||_F
- retention and reference differences add |alpha_a - alpha_a'| ||R_a' - f_a'|| + alpha_a ||R_a - R_a'||
- alignment identity (6.2) holds exactly at every registered and test epsilon
- frame inequality c_max^-1 sum_b ||G_b R||^2 <= ||R||^2 <= c_min^-1 sum_b ||G_b R||^2
- exact relative SD of a Gaussian sketch is at most sqrt(2/k)
- sketched band power is unbiased and its Monte Carlo SD matches the exact formula
- sqrt(2/k) = 0.35 at k = 16 and 0.18 at k = 64
- reach score: ||H(a) - H(A0)|| <= s^_a(H) + [sum_b s_b^2 eps_b]^(1/2) ||H|| (L_U = 1)

*Scope:* Exact eigendecompositions of small graphs; global spectral grid bounds include a derivative-based remainder and one-sided window boundaries. Float64 references are not interval-arithmetic certificates. The tightness ratio of Figure S18c is a separate empirical audit.

### Proposition 7: Model-free one-step regret under support qualification

*Source:* main Eqs. (7.1)-(7.2); Supplementary Tables S7, S28 and S28b.

On the simultaneous accuracy event Delta(pi_one) <= min_a Delta(a) + 2 max_a e(a) <= 2 max_a e(a) when A0 is supported; e(n) = 2B sqrt(log(2|A|/delta)/(2n)) (Hoeffding) and the empirical-Bernstein radius e_B(n) cover simultaneously; ESS >= 64 forces omega_max <= 0.125.

Verified:

- on the accuracy event Delta(pi_one) <= min_a Delta + 2 max e <= 2 max e (A0 supported)
- Hoeffding and empirical-Bernstein radii cover all actions simultaneously at 1 - delta
- main text: the regret bound 2e at n_min = 64 is 0.087 nats
- Table S28b Hoeffding column 2e(n) at n = 64, 74, 91, 100, 142
- 2e(n) <= 0.003 needs about 53,000 units (8 B^2 log(2|A|/delta)/0.003^2)
- empirical-Bernstein radius falls below Hoeffding's for n >~ 95 (sigma_1 = 0.007)
- 2 e_B(n) <= 0.003 at n ~ 3,000 for sigma_1 = 0.007
- omega_max <= 1/sqrt(ESS) on one weight vector
- ESS >= 64 gives omega_max <= 0.125; ESS >= 32 gives <= 0.177 (Tables S7, S18)

*Scope:* Uniform weights and independent logged units, as the statement requires; self-normalized weights are excluded by the statement itself.

### Proposition 8: Approximate search regret

*Source:* main Section 2; Supplementary Note S20.

If sup_a |J^(a) - J(a)| <= e_H and the search returns a zeta_H-approximate minimizer of J^, then J(a^) - min_a J(a) <= 2 e_H + zeta_H.

Verified:

- J(a^) - min J <= 2 e_H + zeta_H
- the bound is attained when J^ ties a good and a bad sequence

*Scope:* Random finite sequence families; e_H is a supremum, not a per-step RMSE.

### Proposition 9: Conditional action stability and selective sensing

*Source:* main Section 2; Supplementary Note S23 and Algorithm S3.

If the gap between the two smallest scores at the predicted state exceeds 2 L_J r and the supported set is invariant on the ball, the minimizing action is the same at every state of the ball.

Verified:

- gap > 2 L_J r certifies one minimizer on the whole ball

*Scope:* Region containment and support, recovery, budget and search invariance are premises. The check only tests fixed finite families of linear scores; it does not generate a trained-runtime certificate.

### Lemma 3 (Supplementary): Work bound of Algorithm S3

*Source:* Supplementary Algorithm S3, Lemma 3 (Note S22) and Figure S11.

With declared upper bounds on every operation, a feasible budget W >= C_qC(x), W_C >= C_qC(x) and C_pred <= W_C, the invariant w + W_C <= W holds after every paid operation and every branch that returns a prediction uses at most W; the infeasible branch pays nothing.

Verified:

- cm_experiments.budget: total work <= W on every branch with a prediction; infeasible pays nothing
- all four terminal statuses are exercised (not full decision-event coverage)
- observed work above a declared bound is refused rather than credited
- Figure S11: releasing the reserve before the final site can exceed W *(reference value)*
- the executable rule and the reference agree on paid operations, actions, decision counts and total work

*Scope:* Synthetic backends whose observed work never exceeds declared bounds. Four terminal statuses, paid-operation order, executed actions, acquisition/recovery counts and work are compared with the reference. Certificate premises are supplied by the synthetic cases; no learned-controller certificate or full benchmark path is established.

### Proposition 10: Budget-matched decision boundary

*Source:* main Section 2 and Figure 6; Supplementary Note S25 and Table S47.

(i) At a common ceiling q_pred beats q_FB iff phi > 1 and q_B iff phi > r_B; (ii) with ensemble spend the crossovers become 1 - b(o - o_dec)/g and r_B - [b(o - o_dec) - b(o - o_B)]/g; (iii) under priced work feedback is preferred iff lambda < (1 - phi) g / [EC(q_FB) - EC(q_pred)].

Verified:

- (i) contract crossovers 1 and r_B
- (ii) ensemble-spend crossover against q_FB
- (ii) ensemble-spend crossover against q_B
- (iii) priced-work crossover lambda*_pred

*Scope:* The additive ensemble-spend model of (ii) is a stated sensitivity assumption.

### Proposition 11: Comparator-relative advantage decomposition

*Source:* main Eq. (31); Supplementary Note S21.

V^pi_0 - V^C_0 = E_pi sum_l A^C_l(h_l, a_l) for every policy executing from the same initial history.

Verified:

- V^pi_0 - V^C_0 = E_pi sum_l A^C_l(h_l, a_l) (history-dependent, open-loop and nominal comparators)

*Scope:* Exact enumeration of finite-horizon processes with history-dependent stochastic policies. The current ActionCritic targets nominal-relative Eq. (13), not the comparator-relative advantage of Eq. (31).

### Eqs. (5)-(6): Training-only entry contract and log-depth-integrated loss

*Source:* main Eqs. (5)-(6); Supplementary Tables S3-S4.

DIL_log d is the trapezoid rule in log2 depth normalized by log2(d_K/d_1); the six gates of Eq. (5) with eps_plant = 0.004, tau_PDD = 1.0, tau_DIL = 0.020, tau_sup = 0.80 and eps_headroom = 0.003.

Verified:

- log-depth-integrated loss equals the NumPy reference trapezoid rule in log2 depth
- the six registered gates and thresholds decide entry

*Scope:* The Table S4 decisions are replayed by scripts/check_si_identities.py.

### Eqs. (32)-(33): Expected-cost identity and branch accounting

*Source:* main Eqs. (32)-(33); Supplementary Note S22 and Table S23.

E C = C_g + p0 C_C,0 + (1 - p0)[(1 - p1) C_S + p1 (C_A + C_C,1)] reduces to (1 - p_fallback) C_controller + p_fallback C_qC for the deployed rules (C_g = 0, p1 = 0).

Verified:

- branch-weighted mean cost converges to the accounting identity
- with C_g = 0 and p1 = 0 Eq. (33) reduces to (1 - p) C_controller + p C_qC

*Scope:* Expectation over mutually exclusive branches, checked against simulated branch frequencies.

### Note S19: Action cost model and admissible truncation order

*Source:* Supplementary Note S19; Tables S6c and S44.

m(T) = (1 + r + s + f_res r (T - 1))/(1 + r); T <= 1 + [m (1 + r) - (1 + r + s)]/(f_res r); full-state degree-8 sensing costs 8r/(1 + r) of a nominal step; the S44 tail model is C_qC [1 + o_fix + f v] with v = r (T - 1)/(1 + r).

Verified:

- the admissible truncation order inverts the per-member multiplier
- the admissible resolvent fraction inverts the per-member multiplier
- sensing at period 2 costs half of full-state sensing at every site
- registered resolvent polynomials have maximum power T (runtime sparse-work counting is separate)

*Scope:* A floating-point work model; memory traffic and wall time are outside it.

### Note S24: Two resampling sources and inference for the comparison

*Source:* main Section 2 and Methods; Supplementary Note S24 and Tables S14b, S42.

Var D_bar = sigma_u^2/J + sigma_v^2/S + sigma_e^2/(J S); the balanced two-way mean squares give Var^_unbiased(D_bar) = (MS_graph + MS_seed - MS_e)/(J S); nonnegative reporting estimates are separate. Minimum detectable effects are 2.80 SE (two-sided 0.05) and 3.34 SE at the first Holm step of four; equivalence uses two one-sided tests at the margin.

Verified:

- Var^(D_bar) = (MS_graph + MS_seed - MS_e)/(J S)
- the untruncated two-way moment estimate of Var D_bar is unbiased
- V_test - V_graph <= sigma_v^2/S, so 1 - rho^-2 lower-bounds the seed share
- minimum detectable effects 2.80 SE (two-sided 0.05) and 3.34 SE (first Holm step of four)
- two one-sided tests keep their size at the margin boundary
- Holm adjustment agrees with cross_morse.statistics and cm_campaigns.numeric

*Scope:* Balanced designs; the crossed seed-by-unit bootstrap of the campaign is a separate estimator.
